intro: Argentina is a federal presidential republic of 23 provinces and the autonomous city of Buenos Aires. It has been a democracy since 1983.

chapters.title: President and Congress
text: The president is elected for four years and can serve two terms in a row. The president works from the Casa Rosada, the 'Pink House', in Buenos Aires.

Congress has a Chamber of Deputies, shared out by population, and a Senate with three senators from each province and the city of Buenos Aires. Voting is compulsory from 18 to 70, and 16- and 17-year-olds may vote if they wish.

chapters.title: Rights and reforms
text: In 2010 Argentina became the first country in Latin America to allow same-sex marriage, and abortion was legalised in 2020 after a huge campaign by young women wearing green scarves.

chapters.title: Flag and national days
text: The flag has light blue and white stripes with the golden Sun of May in the centre. National holidays include 25 May, for the May Revolution, and 9 July, Independence Day.

chapters.title: Argentina in the world
text: Argentina is a member of the G20 and a founding member of Mercosur. It continues to claim the Falkland Islands through diplomacy, and its relationships with neighbours such as Brazil and Chile are among the most important.

keyTerms.meaning: One of the large regions into which Argentina is divided, each with its own government.
A system where power is shared between the national government and provinces or states.
